title: Full PQS Asset Entity Schema - 82+ Field Data Model

context.problem_statement: The pqs/asset entity schema in the model-vue codebase only explicitly defined ~15 fields (entity$, id, tag, xco, yco, zco, building, level, room, atype, map, custom12-19). The actual production asset data model used by PQS deployments includes 82+ fields covering custom fields (1-32), data fields (1-20), department hierarchies (1-10), filter hierarchies, disciplines, line/piping references, and polygon geometry for Room/Area asset types. This gap between the production data contract and the codebase schema meant new developers, AI agents, and the backup delivery plane (DEC-000019) had no authoritative field reference, risking silent data loss on export/import and incomplete asset rendering.

options: Full explicit Asset interface with all 82+ named fields plus JSON Schema (chosen)
Minimal interface with [key: string]: any catch-all only
Field enum/constant list without TypeScript typing
External schema file (OpenAPI/Swagger) with no in-code types
outcome: Define the complete pqs/asset entity schema with all 82+ fields explicitly typed across three artifacts: (1) TypeScript Asset interface in components.ts with named fields grouped by category, (2) JSON Schema at provenance/schema/pqs-asset.schema.json for validation, (3) updated SPEC-000003 bundle_entity_schema with csv_output_order and field group documentation. Room/Area asset types include the poly field (number[][]) for polygon geometry. The [key: string]: any catch-all is retained for forward compatibility.
rationale: Explicit field definitions provide: type safety for consumers accessing asset properties, IDE autocomplete for all 82+ fields, a single source of truth for the CSV import/export column order, JSON Schema validation for bundle generation (SPEC-000003), documentation for the filter hierarchy (filtertop/filterside/filtersubside/filtersubside2) and department/discipline/custom/data field ranges. The catch-all index signature is kept so existing code using dynamic key access continues to work without breakage. Field spellings (dicipline, preceededby, followeby) match the production database column names exactly - renaming would be a breaking change requiring a separate migration decision.

risk.acceptance: This is an additive schema expansion - no fields are removed or renamed. Existing code that only accesses tag, custom12, xco, yco etc. is unaffected. The [key: string]: any catch-all means the TypeScript compiler will not reject any existing dynamic access patterns. The only risk is if a field name in the schema does not match the actual DynamoDB column name, which would cause silent data misses. Mitigated by deriving field names from production asset data samples.

identity_core.notes: entity$ is always '-/pqs/asset'. id is UUID. tag is primary identifier.

positioning.notes: xco/yco are pixel coordinates (string or number). map is string index. zco is null for 2D.

classification.notes: atype is the primary asset type classifier (e.g. 'Room/Area', 'Valve').

location.notes: building and level are structural; room is the specific area name.

filter_hierarchy.notes: Four-level filter hierarchy used by BasicSide filter UI.

disciplines.notes: Spelling matches production DB column names (dicipline, not discipline).

grouping.notes: Asset group name for logical grouping.

departments.notes: Ten department slots for hierarchical department classification.

custom_fields.notes: custom12 is used as tag alias in search/display. custom19 often holds reference codes.

data_fields.notes: Generic data fields for tenant-specific metadata.

line_piping.notes: Line/piping references. Spellings match production DB (preceededby, followeby).

geometry.notes: Polygon coordinates for Room/Area asset types only. Array of [x,y] pairs.

point_asset.description: Standard assets positioned by xco/yco coordinates on a map level

room_area_asset.description: Room/Area assets that include polygon geometry for spatial boundaries
room_area_asset.geometry: poly field with array of [x,y] coordinate pairs defining the boundary polygon
room_area_asset.notes: xco/yco represent the centroid or label position. poly defines the rendered boundary.
